ZARA SOUZA

Helsinki, Finland | zara.souza@mail.example

---

EDUCATION

M.Sc. Electrical Engineering, Charles River Institute of Technology (CRIT), 2018
Thesis: Wideband Array Calibration Methods for L-Band Receive Chains

---

WORK EXPERIENCE

Polaris RF Labs -- Signal Processing Engineer
January 2019 -- present

- Designed and implemented the embedded digital signal processing firmware in C++ for the PRF-440 digital receiver module, running on a Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ SoC under hard real-time constraints (8 ms processing window per pulse repetition interval, zero-copy DMA transfers, deterministic memory management).

- Developed and maintain the production Python calibration and regression-test framework (pytest-based, approximately 12,000 lines of code) used by the hardware verification team across 14 automated test stations. The framework runs nightly CI jobs and produces go/no-go reports for every receiver board before shipment.

- Sole engineer responsible for the English-language technical documentation suite: interface control documents, acceptance-test procedures, and customer delivery reports. All cross-site coordination with our partner in Delft conducted in English.

- Currently based in Helsinki; relocating to Oulu in Q1 2027 (two-month notice period, apartment search in progress).

---

PROJECTS

Polar-SAR Ground Processor (2022--2023)
Developed the range-compression and azimuth-focusing pipeline for a Finnish Orbital Programme Office-funded synthetic aperture radar ground segment. Characterised the receive chain's gain flatness and group delay across the 1.27 GHz bandwidth using a Keysight PNA-X network analyser, feeding the resulting calibration tables into the processor's range-matched filter. The SAR payload is designed for a polar-orbiting microsatellite; I wrote the on-ground processing chain that handles its downlinked raw echo data. Work carried out from Helsinki under my permanent Finnish residence permit (A-permit, obtained 2021).

CRIT Thesis -- Wideband Array Calibration (2017--2018)
Master's thesis on mutual-coupling-aware calibration of a 64-element L-band receive array, combining near-field chamber probe measurements with an embedded element-pattern model to reduce calibration error by 4.2 dB relative to the conventional isolated-element assumption. This work established the electrical engineering foundations in array signal processing that my subsequent career has built on directly.

---

SKILLS

- Phased-array and beamforming signal processing: designed the digital beamforming architecture for Polaris RF Labs' 32-channel coherent receive array, including per-channel gain/phase equalisation, sum-and-delay beam steering, and sidelobe-control weighting
- C/C++ (embedded, bare-metal and RTOS), VHDL
- MATLAB, Simulink
- Linux (Yocto, Petalinux), Git, Jenkins CI
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Hiring Manager
Kaikuvaara Oy
Oulu, Finland

18 September 2026

Re: Senior Signal Processing Engineer

Over the past seven years at Polaris RF Labs I have built, tested, and shipped the signal-processing chain for three generations of digital receiver hardware -- from the C++ firmware running on the SoC to the Python framework that verifies every board before it leaves the factory. I am applying for the Senior Signal Processing Engineer position at Kaikuvaara because the work you do sits at the same intersection of analogue RF and digital processing that I have spent my career in, and because Oulu is where I want to be next.

The deliverables I am most useful for are the ones that survived contact with real hardware. At Polaris I wrote the complete embedded DSP chain for the PRF-440 receiver under an 8 ms real-time budget, which meant solving problems that only appear when the code runs on an actual FPGA-ARM hybrid -- DMA contention, cache-coherence faults, timing jitter that a desktop simulation never reproduces. I also built the production calibration framework that exercises every shipped board against its specification; that framework has run unattended on 14 test stations for four years and has caught two silent hardware regressions before any customer saw them.

The project most directly relevant to Kaikuvaara's instrument work was the Polar-SAR ground processor I developed in 2022-23. I wrote the range-compression and azimuth-focusing pipeline for a microsatellite SAR payload, including the RF calibration measurements that feed its matched filter. That project gave me end-to-end exposure from antenna element to final image, and it taught me the discipline that spaceborne data demands: there are no second passes on a downlinked data set, so the processing has to be right the first time.

Beyond the SAR work, the beamforming system I designed for Polaris's latest 32-channel receiver is the piece of engineering I am most proud of: per-channel equalisation, adaptive sidelobe control, and sum-and-delay beam steering, all running in real time on a single Zynq SoC. The challenge was not any one algorithm but making them coexist within the timing and memory budget, which is the kind of systems-level integration that I find most engaging and that I expect instrument-level work at Kaikuvaara requires.

I hold a permanent Finnish residence permit and am already in the process of relocating to Oulu -- I have visited the city several times and have started looking at apartments in the Linnanmaa area. My notice period at Polaris RF Labs is two months.

What I would bring to Kaikuvaara is a track record of delivering real-time signal-processing systems on real hardware, documented and tested well enough that other engineers can maintain them after I have moved on. I am used to owning a processing chain end to end, from algorithm design through firmware implementation through the test suite that proves it works. I have attached my CV and would be happy to discuss any of the above in more detail.

Zara Souza

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
